newsitem.title: USA: Clinton opposes bid to reverse Mexico drug ruling.
newsitem.headline: Clinton opposes bid to reverse Mexico drug ruling.

text.p: President Bill Clinton is convinced that his certification of Mexico's efforts in the war against drugs was correct and opposes congressional efforts to reverse it, his spokesman said on Friday.
A House of Representatives committee voted on Thursday to overturn Clinton's finding that Mexico was fully cooperating in the anti-drug fight. The full House was expected to vote on the measure.
Clinton "takes strong issue with the House committee," White House Press Secretary Mike McCurry told reporters.
"The president believes certification was the right decision ... this is the best way to encourage better and stronger cooperation in the fight against drugs," McCurry said.

Over administration objections, the International Relations Committee voted 27-5 to send the measure overturning Clinton's finding to the full House for action. Similar legislation has been introduced in the Senate.

Under a 1961 law, congressional disapproval of Clinton's certification that Mexico is an anti-drug ally automatically triggers a ban on U.S. aid and requires votes against multilateral development bank assistance to Mexico.
But the panel and many members of Congress are unwilling to go that far, fearing such action might provoke Mexico to cut off all cooperation in the fight against drug trafficking.
